Get your laptop ready before Day 1. Plan **30–60 minutes** the day before — not the morning of. The optional [Day 0](Schedule.qmd#day-0-optional-software-setup-computational-refresher) session is the place to bring any install problems you can't solve yourself.

::: callout-important
**Bring your own laptop.** The workshop is hands-on — every participant works on their **own laptop** (at least **16 GB RAM** and **~10 GB free disk**). There are no lab machines, so set everything up below before you arrive.
:::

::: callout-tip
**What you'll have at the end:**

1. R and RStudio installed and working
2. VS Code installed
3. The command-line build tools your operating system needs to compile R packages

Installing the R / Bioconductor packages (plus LaTeX and a Quarto primer) is handled in **[Tutorial 00 — Get Up and Running with R, RStudio & Quarto](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_00_Setup_RStudio_Packages.html)**, which we walk through together at the start of Day 1.
:::

## 1. Required tools

- **R ≥ 4.4** — [download](https://www.r-project.org)
- **RStudio Desktop** (current release) — [download](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)
- **VS Code** (current release) — [download](https://code.visualstudio.com/download)

## 2. Install command-line tools

Several R / Bioconductor packages **compile from source** the first time you install them, which needs a working command-line **compiler toolchain**; the command-line portions of the workshop also assume a POSIX shell. Set this up once, for your operating system. The command line itself — navigating, pipes, `grep` — is covered in [Appendix B](Resources_Folder/Appendix_B_Unix_Command_Line.html) and [Appendix F](Resources_Folder/Appendix_F_GREP_Regex_Shell.html), and the optional [Day 0](Schedule.qmd) walks through it; if a package later fails to build, the [FAQ](FAQ.qmd) lists the usual fixes.

**macOS** — open the built-in **Terminal** (Applications → Utilities), or install [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com/) for a nicer one, then install Apple's Xcode command-line tools:

``` bash
xcode-select --install
```

This provides `clang`, `git`, `make`, and the headers R needs to build packages. Some packages also need a Fortran compiler — if you later hit `gfortran not found`, install [gfortran for macOS](https://mac.r-project.org/tools/). Re-launch RStudio after it finishes.

**Windows** — install **Rtools**, the toolchain that lets Windows build R packages from source, from <https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/> (pick the version matching your R — e.g. Rtools44 for R 4.4). For the shell/command-line portions of the workshop, also install **WSL2 + Ubuntu**, which gives you a real POSIX shell:

1. Run **PowerShell as Administrator**.
2. `wsl --install -d ubuntu` and press Enter. Restart when prompted.
3. Launch **Ubuntu** from the Start menu and set a username and password.
4. `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y`

Full Microsoft guide: <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install>. If you run R *inside* WSL rather than native Windows, see the [FAQ](FAQ.qmd) note on where to keep your project files.

**Linux** — use your built-in terminal and install the build toolchain from your package manager. On Ubuntu/Debian:

``` bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y build-essential gfortran
```

`build-essential` provides `gcc`, `g++`, and `make`; `gfortran` covers packages with Fortran code. On Fedora/RHEL, use `sudo dnf groupinstall "Development Tools"` plus `gcc-gfortran`.

## 3. Install the R packages

The R / Bioconductor packages the workshop uses — along with a short primer on how packages, updates, LaTeX, and Quarto work — are covered in **[Tutorial 00 — Get Up and Running with R, RStudio & Quarto](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_00_Setup_RStudio_Packages.html)**. We do it together at the very start of Day 1, but because the first install can take **20–60 minutes**, we recommend opening Tutorial 00 and running its install block *before* you arrive.

## Something didn't work?

The [FAQ](FAQ.qmd) documents the issues that come up most often: Mac compiler errors, `BiocManager` mirror selection, RStudio caching old library paths, etc.
